title: JNI Local/Global Reference 与跨边界泄漏
key_conclusions: JNI local references are frame-scoped but can still overflow reference tables in loops, so DeleteLocalRef or PushLocalFrame/PopLocalFrame is needed for large batches.
JNI global references strongly keep Java objects alive until DeleteGlobalRef, making them a common cross-boundary retained-object leak source.
Weak global references do not prevent GC and must be promoted with NewLocalRef and null-checked before use.
JNI leak diagnosis requires combining HPROF JNI global roots with meminfo, showmap, heapprofd, fd, thread, and native owner evidence.
shallow_points: The article does not include a real HPROF showing a JNI global root retained path.
It does not validate ART IndirectReferenceTable, CheckJNI, or reference-table diagnostics against a target Android branch.
It does not include a runnable NDK sample that leaks and then fixes a global reference, local reference overflow, and thread detach issue.
It does not correlate a same-run HPROF with heapprofd and showmap artifacts for a real JNI/native leak.
